title: The hedgehog

D0.outcome: States the app's working definition (pawns on b6, d6 and e6 and no c-pawn, against pawns on c4 and e4 and no d-pawn; colours may be reversed) and the idea: a compact set-up behind the sixth rank, waiting for the moment of a break.

D1.outcome: Told the structure, states the cramped side's plan (keep the compact set-up, keep the pieces flexible, wait for ...b5 or ...d5) and the space side's plans (keep the space and prevent the breaks, or strike first).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions decides whether a break is ready, whether to keep waiting, and whether the space side should prevent the break or attack.

D3.outcome: Predicts one-feature changes (a trade of central pieces, a break prepared or not, a space-gaining pawn advance) and checks the verdict with the engine, knowing that engines often rate such positions near equal.

misconceptions: The hedgehog is just a passive, cramped position.
The space side only has to keep still.
sources: sources/sheets/capablanca_chess-fundamentals.md §5 item 17 (the hedgehog is named there from outside knowledge as a counter-example to 'backward pawns lose', flagged CHECK)

rating.note: expert estimate; tier=5; plans recalled, no sheet support, needs a strong-player review

conditions: Working definition (the app's own, not claimed to match any book): one side has pawns on b6, d6 and e6 and none on the c-file, the other has pawns on c4 and e4 and none on the d-file; the colours may be reversed.
The cramped side keeps pieces back and the pawns compact so that no target appears; waiting is a plan only while the opponent cannot make progress without a concession.
The break (...b5 or ...d5) is timed by the opponent's piece placement: play it when the squares it uses are covered; played too early it loses a pawn or opens the position for the space side.
The space side risks overextension, since every advance leaves a weakness behind it, and the structure is the standard case where a backward pawn is a trade-off and not a fault.
contrasts: The cramped side breaks before the pieces are placed: d5 is attacked by c4 and e4, and the pawn is lost.
The cramped side waits while the space side prepares an advance that removes the break: waiting has stopped being a plan.
The same pawn squares but a Black c-pawn is still on the board: this is not the hedgehog.
